title: Alibaba releases Qwen3.8-Flash-Next as an open-weight preview of Qwen 4
subtitle: The 125B-parameter mixture-of-experts model activates only 6B per token and is being positioned as an architecture sneak peek for the next Qwen generation.
author: AESOP AI Engine
body: Alibaba's Qwen team released Qwen3.8-Flash-Next on August 26, 2026 — a 125-billion-parameter mixture-of-experts model that activates only about 6 billion parameters per token. The release pairs the main network with a 51-billion-parameter N-gram embedding and a 4-billion-parameter multi-token prediction module, totaling roughly 180 billion parameters on disk. Weights were posted to Hugging Face and ModelScope, and the production API is priced at $0.16 per million input tokens and $0.47 per million output tokens on Alibaba's QwenCloud.

The release matters because Alibaba is framing it as an architecture preview for Qwen 4 rather than a finished frontier model. Four design choices anchor the paper — a hybrid of Gated DeltaNet and Qwen Sparse Attention, a Gated Residual scheme, N-gram Embedding, and the Muon optimizer — and the same pattern was used a year ago when Qwen3-Next previewed Qwen3.5. Developers get running open weights and a stable API price now, and Alibaba gets a feedback signal on the architecture months before the flagship ships.

The move continues a China-side rhythm that has defined the summer. Qwen 3.8-Max landed at 2.4 trillion parameters on August 3, DeepSeek V4 Flash 0731 shipped at a 40% discount to comparable US frontier calls, and Z.AI's GLM-5.3 Flash arrived on August 26. Six of the top ten public model calls this month are now Chinese, and the open-weights lane — where the model can be run locally and audited — has become the primary lever for that shift.

For learners: the interesting technical detail is the 125B / 6B split. Total parameters set the ceiling on what the model can memorize; active parameters set the cost of each token you generate. A well-designed MoE lets you pay for a small model at inference time while training against the depth of a large one, and that gap is why open-weight labs can undercut closed frontier pricing by an order of magnitude. When you evaluate a model release this year, always look for both numbers — the marketing headline is usually the bigger of the two.
